content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: the best policy-compliant plan, lifting service level to 76.6% for 13:45-17:30 for ₹2,703. It still falls short of the 80% target.","why":"The extra calls come from the MKT-2026-551 loan email, not from a staffing problem. Over the last four intervals there were 307 calls against 236 forecast, mostly loan and new-offer enquiries, and service level fell to 68% at 09:45. With no action, the disruption window is predicted at 72.1%, with the general queue at 63.6%. R1 adds chat deflection on both queues, cancels coaching and moves up to 9 cross-skilled agents from payments to general. That raises the window to 76.6% (general 70.1%, payments 85.3%), cuts abandons from 7.9% to 6.0%, and puts the rest of the day at 81.5%. No policy-compliant option reaches 80% over the window.","trade_offs":["P2 (80.1%, ₹732) and P3 (79.6%, ₹2,307) score higher or cost less. Both rely on an IVR outage message, which breaks policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage or incident.","R2 costs the same ₹2,703 and has slightly fewer abandons (5.6% vs 6.0%), but window service level is a little lower (76.4%, general 69.0%) and it delays breaks.","P1 is free but makes things worse: 69.7%, with general at 60.4%.","Moving agents off payments has little downside here: payments is predicted at 85.3% under R1, up from 83.7% with no action."],"watch":"Watch the general queue. It is predicted at only 70.1% even with R1, so check that chat deflection is actually taking new-offer enquiries from 14:45. Keep payments above 80% once the 6-agent move starts at 16:00. If loan enquiries keep exceeding forecast, consider asking the duty manager about other options, such as asking marketing to clarify the campaign or a policy-compliant message."}
